brief: Goldman Sachs TMT specialist Peter Callahan previews day 1 of the GS Communacopia and Technology Conference (9/8 to 9/11, San Francisco) and reprints a Friday sentiment check. The argued chain: TMT fundamentals kept improving through 2Q earnings (NVDA guiding FY27 revenues above 70% y/y, AVGO pointing to 100%+ growth in 2027 and 2028), yet price action was choppier, with the GS TMT 12-month Momentum Pair down more than 10% in August as semis lagged the broader market and software. Callahan attributes the gap to a complicated macro backdrop (rates watch into a live FOMC this month) and muted risk appetite (volumes, VIX, gross exposures), leaving investors to debate what else the market needs to re-engage the AI trade, or whether it is signalling a regime shift away from the capex trade. Subsector reads follow: semis most loved, hardware controversial, software bifurcated toward inference economy names over SaaS and Apps, internet choppy, telcos bid and cable out of favor. The note maps debates and desk sentiment. It sets no price targets and makes no recommendations.
